questions.question: People in ancient India believed that when the ‘_______’ ritual was performed with the help of Brahmanas, it led to the rebirth of the sacrificer as a Kshatriya, even if he was not one by birth.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Hiranya-garbha.__**​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Hiranyagarbha ritual was performed with the help of Brahmin to declare the king as Kshatriya, even if he is not one by birth.
 
• When this ritual was performed, it was thought to lead to the "rebirth" of the sacrifice as a Kshatriya, even if he is not one by birth.
 
• This ritual was prominent among the kings in mid-7th and 8th centuries.
 
• **Samavaj-Tana**
 
 
• **​**It is also known as the “Snana” ritual. Samavartana generally means graduation.
 
• It is a ceremony performed by the students at the end of their studentship.
 
• It marks the end of the education course.
 
• It is similar to present-day convocation or felicitation ceremony.
 
 
 
• **Upanayana**
 
 
• It is a Hindu ritual, particularly for boys of the Brahmin community.
 
• In this ceremony, Brahmin boys wear sacred thread for the first time.
 
 
 
• **Medhajanana**
 
 
• Medhajanana ritual is performed to evoke divine help in the sharpening of the intelligence, memory, and tenacious power of the student.
 
• A student would become a scholar and a responsible man if he acts up to the symbolism and suggestions of this ritual.
 
• Medhajanana is the production of intelligence in a baby. This rite is performed the very next day after the birth of a baby.​​
 
 

 

4a:T13

questions.question: In which of the following are the dance movements characterised by bent legs, while feet keep rhythm?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bharatnatyam.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bharatanatyam **is a dance of **Tamil Nadu** in southern India.

 
 
• It traces its origins back to the Natyashastra, an ancient treatise on theatre written by the mythic priest Bharata.
 
• Originally a temple dance for women, Bharatanatyam often is used to express Hindu religious stories and devotions.
 
• It was not commonly seen on the public stage until the 20th century.
 
• **The dance movements are characterized by bent legs, while feet keep rhythm**.
 
• Hands may be used in a series of mudras, or symbolic hand gestures, to tell a story.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Manipuri **comes from Manipur in northeastern India.

 
 
• It has its roots in that state’s folk traditions and rituals and often depicts scenes from the life of the god Krishna.
 
• Unlike some of the other, more rhythmic dances, Manipuri is characterized by smooth and graceful movements.
 
• Female roles are especially fluid in the arms and hands, while male roles tend to have more forceful movements.
 
• The dance may be accompanied by narrative chanting and choral singing.
 
 
 
• **Kathakali **comes from southwestern India, around the state of **Kerala**.
 
 
• Like Bharatanatyam, kathakali is a religious dance.
 
• It draws inspiration from the Ramayana and stories from Shaiva traditions.
 
• Kathakali is traditionally performed by boys and men, even for female roles.
 
• The costumes and makeup are especially elaborate, with faces made to look like painted masks and enormous headdresses.
 
 
 
• A dance of northern India, **Kathak **is often a dance of love.
 
 
• It is performed by both men and women.
 
• The movements include intricate footwork accented by bells worn around the ankles and stylized gestures adapted from normal body language.
 
• It was originated by Kathakas, a professional storyteller who used a mixture of dance, song, and drama.
 
• Like other Indian dances, it began as a temple dance but soon moved into the courts of ruling houses.

questions.question: Which of the following dance forms was introduced by the great Vaishnava saint and reformer Mahapurusha Sankaradeva?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sattriya**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sattriya** is a **dance-drama performance art** of the 15th-century **Bhakti movement** introduced by **Mahapurusha Sankaradeva**. 
 
• The plays of **Sattriya** are called **Ankiya nat**.
 
• It is usually performed in the **Namghar** of monastery temples **(Sastras****).**
 
• The themes of the plays are** Lord Krishna** and other avatars of Lord Vishnu.
 
• The **Sangeet Natak Akademi** of India recognized** Sattriya**** as a classical dance in 2000**.​ 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **​******Srimanta****** Sankardev, **born in 1449 was an **Assamese Polymath**.
 
• He wrote **Six Ankiya Nat**.
 
• Among the Ankiya Nat** Cinha Yatra** was the most Famous.
 
• The famous poetic composition** Kirtan Ghosa **was his creation.

questions.question: The snake boat race is a unique feature of which of the following festivals?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Onam.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Boat races of Kerala are a special feature of Onam.**
 
• Onam is the **harvest festival** **of Kerala** which is celebrated to welcome King Mahabali.
 
• Depending on the Malayalam Calendar, the festival falls in the month of** August or September **and lasts for **4-10 days.**
 
• Celebrations involve songs, dance, games, and feasts.
 
• **The Snake Boat Race called Vallamkali **is carried out on the** Pampa river** with hundreds of people racing and chanting folk songs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kalinga Festival**

 
 
• ​**Kalinga Mahotsav** is one of the most famous festivals of** Orissa.**
 
• It holds great religious significance for people.
 
• The aim of this festival is **to encourage people to follow the path of peace and calm,** rather than fighting amongst themselves.
 
• The** Vishwa Shanti Stupa,** also called the Peace Pagoda, serves as the **venue **of the Kalinga Mahotsav.
 
 
 
• **Bhogali Bihu**
 
 
• ​Magh Bihu or Bhogali Bihu is a **celebration of bountiful nature and abundance.**
 
• It is also an **occasion for the people of Assam to enjoy (bhog kora)** and share in the gifts of nature as a community, and strengthen a sense of identity and belonging.
 
 
 
• **Dussehra**
 
 
• ​Dussehra, also called Dasara or** Vijayadashami, in Hinduism.**
 
• The Festival marks the **triumph of Lord Rama,** an avatar of Vishnu, over the **10-headed demon king Ravana**, who abducted Lord Rama's wife, Sita. 
 
 

40:T

questions.question: As a part of the celebration of the Navroz festival by Parsi community, a deity named Meher is worshipped. This deity is the presiding deity of the:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** __Moon.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Parsi New Year is thought to have started **being observed from around 3,500 BCE, according to** historians and academics.**
 
• The events commemorated the founding of the Zoroastrian religion in Iran by **Prophet Zarathustra.** Navroz represents the cosmos' rebirth to the **adherents of this religion.**
 
• They consider **Ahura Mazda to be the name of a single invisible God.** They offer fire, a representation of light, as a sacrifice to their god. The Indian Gujarati town of Udvada is the** holy location for Parsis.**
 
• On **Navroz, Parsis visit the synagogue three times **to worship Khorshed and Meher, the two deities who rule over the **sun and moon,** **respectively.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A Parsi New Year is known as **Jamshed-e-Navroz, **according to the House Captain. It is observed on the first day of the first month of the Zoroastrian faith calendar, known as the Shehenshahi. The celebration** honours rebirth and renewal.**
 
• **Parsis clean and use rangolis** made of jasmine and rose flowers to beautify their homes. India's Parsis are a minority religious group.
 
• They travelled from Iran to the **region of Gujarat.**
 
• Mumbai is home to a **sizable portion of the Parsi people.** They identify as Zoroastrian believers, an Iranian prophet. The Zend Avesta is the **holy text of the Parsis.**

questions.question: Which of the following states celebrates a state festival named ‘Bathukamma’?
questions.solution:
The correct amswer is __**Telengana.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bathukamma** is a Hindu deity festival that is mostly observed in** Telangana and certain areas of Andhra Pradesh.**
 
• Bathukamma is a** colourful and flamboyant Telangana** celebration celebrated by women, using flowers native to each district.
 
• This celebration represents **Telangana's cultural character.**
 
• Bathukamma appears in the** later half of the monsoon season**, just before the arrival of winter.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Every year, this festival is observed for nine days, beginning with** Mahalaya Amavasya and ending with Durgashtami,** in September-October of the Gregorian calendar.
 
• Bathukamma originally meant** "life festival" and was held to honour Goddess Parvati **for her blessings on the crop harvest and revenue she helped produce this (current) year, as well as to solicit her blessing for the following year.

questions.question: With which of the following states is the 'Banganga' Festival associated?

• Its name is based on a holy water tank named **Banganga Tank in the Walkeshwar Temple complex at Malabar Hills**.

• **The Banganga tank** is constructed along with the temple for** water conservation**.

questions.question: Prayers during Chhath Puja in Bihar are dedicated to ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__the sun.__**

**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Prayers during **Chhath Puja** in **Bihar **are dedicated to the** Sun God.**
 
• In Bihar, the festival dedicated to Sun and Chhathi Maiya (Mother Shashti or Usha) is celebrated with rigorous and strict manners of preparation.
 
• The Sun is worshipped as the prime source of energy that sustains all lives on the Earth.
 
• Usha and Pratyusha are the two wives that are considered the energy of the Sun God Himself.
 
• The first offering, evening Arghya is offered to Pratyusha, the last ray of the Sun God; and the morning Arghya is offered to Usha, the first ray of the Sun.
 
• It is believed that Chhath Puja was also performed by Karna, the son of Lord Surya and the king of Anga Desh, which is the modern-day Bhagalpur in Bihar.
 
• According to another legend, Pandavas and Draupadi also performed the Puja to overcome obstacles in their lives and reclaim their lost kingdom.​

questions.question: ''Yakshagana' is popular form of dance-drama of :
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Southern India.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• Yakshagana is a traditional theater form of **Karnataka.**
 
• Its literal meaning is 'Yaksha's song'.
 
• It developed in the** Udupi district of Karnataka.**
 
• Its origin is believed to be between the 10th and 16th centuries.
 
• It is a temple art form depicting mythological stories, the Ramayana, the Mahabharata, the Bhagavata, and other Hindu epics.
 
• It is strongly influenced by the Vaishnava Bhakti movement.
 
• It is performed with elaborate headgear, elaborate facial makeup, and vibrant costumes and jewelry.
 
• It is usually sung in Kannada.
 
• It is sung in Malayalam as well as in Tulu.
 
• **So, it is from South India.**

questions.question: The traditional art of embroidery unique to the weavers of Lucknow is called ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**chikankari.**____** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• It is very **intricate and delicate threadwork **done on the muslin clothes originally.
 
• Nowadays the work is being used to decorate a wide variety of fabrics.
 
• There are many views regarding the origin of this embroidery style:
 
 
• Some believe that it originated in **Persia** and was taught to Indians by a Persian trader.
 
• Other sources state that the art has been mentioned in accounts of** Magasthenes which date back to the 3rd century BC**, hence it originated in India only.
 
• Meanwhile,** Noor Jahan, the queen of Jahangir** is also accredited with the introduction of** Chikankari to India**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Phulkari –

 
 
• ​It was first originated in** Punjab**.
 
• It is usually done on the** chaddar or shawls**.
 
• The word Phulkari itself means** ‘flower work’ or a bed of flowers**.
 
• It is mainly a domestic craft, executed by the girls and ladies of the household and sometimes by women servants under their directions.
 
• The embroidery is done on coarse cotton or khaddar material with untwisted silk floss called pat.
 
 
 
• **Kashida kari**.
 
 
• The Kashida motifs used to create this type of embroidery include images inspired by nature.
 
• such as vines, birds, leaves and flowers and this is one of the defining aspects of Kashida embroidery.
 
 
 
• **Zardoji.**
 
 
• Zardozi - It is a type of **heavy and elaborate metal embroidery on silk, satin, or velvet fabric base**.
 
• The centres of Zardozi art are** Lucknow, Bhopal, Delhi, Agra, Kashmir, Ajmer, and Chennai**.
